anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiology data into BIDS, used for formatting; it does not describe this paired-associates stimulation dataset.

anchors.paper_title: iEEG-BIDS, extending the Brain Imaging Data Structure specification to human intracranial electrophysiology
anchors.reason: iEEG-BIDS is a specification for organizing intracranial EEG data, which this BIDS dataset follows; it does not describe this paired-associates dataset.

metadata.methods_description: Each session consisted of 25 lists of encoding, distractor, and cued recall phases. During encoding, 6 word pairs were shown sequentially (4000 ms each, 1000 ms ISI). During cued recall, one word from each pair was presented as a cue with 5000 ms allowed for vocal recall. Open-loop electrical stimulation was delivered to a single electrode (hippocampus or entorhinal cortex) during encoding or retrieval on designated lists, with parameters (anode/cathode, amplitude, pulse frequency, pulse width, pulse count) recorded in behavioral event files. Stimulation began 200 ms before and ended 400 ms after stimulus/cue presentation, lasting 4.6 seconds total. Intracranial recordings were obtained using Blackrock and Medtronic systems, with monopolar and bipolar referencing schemes provided.
